doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: The Tonight Show band personalities and photo
summary: The superstar players who kept to cliques; discussion of a trumpet section photo.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Then it came round. And I feel, and this has nothing to do with me it has to do with Torrie Zito and a lot of the guys that wrote for me so much — Dick Lee played bass trombone and still writes for me for the symphony. That was an unbelievable band, because they were all superstars in their own right and they were horrible to get along with because at the time they didn’t speak to each other. You know, I mean everybody had their own two-person clique.
Yeah. And I had about seven trumpet players, Jimmy Maxwell was another.
I wanted to show you a photo here that Bob Rosengarden gave us. It’s got quite a decent trumpet section there.
Yeah, that’s Doc and Clark and Snooky, yeah, Bob and—
Marian McPartland there. The bari player?
